1: //! Crew's color themes. A single `Theme` struct holds every UI colour, and
2: //! nine `&'static` presets fill it across four families: paper (the e-ink
3: //! reader look crew started as), sepia, the modern Gemini/Codex glow, and
4: //! three phosphor tubes. The active theme lives behind a lock-free `AtomicU8`
5: //! so the winit render thread can read it every frame without blocking. No
6: //! dependencies and no knowledge of the other crates — they import this one.
7: //!
8: //! Most of a palette is DERIVED rather than picked: the text ladder by
9: //! [`ramp`], the terminal slots by [`ansi`], the search wash by [`highlight`],
10: //! the attention colour by [`signal`]. Each of those modules holds the
11: //! shipped presets to what it produces, so the palettes and the system cannot
12: //! drift apart — which is exactly what they had done every time one of those
13: //! modules had to be written.
14: use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicBool, AtomicU64, AtomicU8, Ordering};
15: use std::sync::Mutex;

92:     pub modern: Option<ModernStyle>,

123: impl Theme {
124:     /// Whether this palette is a phosphor tube. Scanlines are the tell: every theme carries a
125:     /// [`CrtStyle`] now (the bloom chain draws the gradient ring's halo), so "has one" says
126:     /// nothing, and a glowing paper theme sets them to zero.
127:     ///
128:     /// Lives here rather than only on [`ThemeId`] because callers that hold a `Theme` used to
129:     /// re-derive it — `ansi.rs` carried its own copy of the old rule and silently disagreed the
130:     /// moment the rule changed.
131:     pub fn is_tube(&self) -> bool {
132:         self.crt.is_some_and(|c| c.scanline > 0.0)
133:     }
134: }

147: /// WCAG 2.1 relative luminance of an sRGB colour — how much light it
148: /// actually emits, which is not what its bytes look like. The basis of
149: /// [`contrast_ratio`], and of which way the renderer's text-gamma curve
150: /// bends for a given pair of colours.
151: pub fn relative_luminance(c: (u8, u8, u8)) -> f32 {
152:     let lin = |c: u8| -> f32 {
153:         let x = c as f32 / 255.0;
154:         if x <= 0.03928 {
155:             x / 12.92
156:         } else {
157:             ((x + 0.055) / 1.055).powf(2.4)
158:         }
159:     };
160:     0.2126 * lin(c.0) + 0.7152 * lin(c.1) + 0.0722 * lin(c.2)
161: }
162: 
163: /// WCAG 2.1 contrast ratio between two sRGB colours.
164: pub fn contrast_ratio(a: (u8, u8, u8), b: (u8, u8, u8)) -> f32 {
165:     let l1 = relative_luminance(a);
166:     let l2 = relative_luminance(b);
167:     let (hi, lo) = if l1 > l2 { (l1, l2) } else { (l2, l1) };
168:     (hi + 0.05) / (lo + 0.05)
169: }

384: /// Rotation mode: when set, the active theme changes every [`ROTATE_MS`]
385: /// within the mode's pool. Stored as a lock-free u8 for per-frame reads:
386: /// 0 = off, 1 = dark pool, 2 = light pool, 3 = auto (pool follows
387: /// [`auto_dark`]).
388: static MODE: AtomicU8 = AtomicU8::new(0);
389: /// Wall-clock ms of the last rotation (or of enabling a mode).
390: static ROTATED_MS: AtomicU64 = AtomicU64::new(0);
391: /// The OS appearance, fed by winit's ThemeChanged. Defaults to dark so a
392: /// platform that never reports stays on the dark pool.
393: static OS_DARK: AtomicBool = AtomicBool::new(true);
394: /// Whether the OS switches its own appearance between light and dark (macOS
395: /// System Settings → Appearance → Auto). Defaults to `true` — on a platform
396: /// crew cannot ask, the OS appearance is taken as authoritative and nothing
397: /// about `auto` changes. It matters only for the `false` case: an appearance
398: /// PINNED to dark never turns light, so following it would make `auto` a
399: /// synonym for `dark` forever, which is exactly the "auto is stuck on dark in
400: /// broad daylight" report this flag exists to answer.
401: static OS_AUTO: AtomicBool = AtomicBool::new(true);
402: /// Whether the local clock currently reads as daytime (the app's light-hours
403: /// window — see `daylight` in crew-app). Consulted ONLY while `OS_AUTO` is
404: /// false. Defaults to false so an unfed clock keeps the historical dark bias.
405: static DAYLIGHT: AtomicBool = AtomicBool::new(false);
406: /// How long each rotated theme is shown: 10 minutes (fonts share this).
407: pub const ROTATE_MS: u64 = 600_000;

409: /// A rotating theme: each mode owns a pool of palettes and cycles through them
410: /// every [`ROTATE_MS`]. These ARE crew's themes now — the individual palettes
411: /// (`PAPER_DARK`, `CRT_GREEN`, …) are the pool members, no longer offered on
412: /// their own. There are exactly THREE pools — `dark`, `light` and `crt` — and
413: /// a palette's own appearance decides which it is in: the modern (Gemini /
414: /// Codex look) palettes are dark and light pages like any other and rotate
415: /// inside `dark` / `light` rather than standing apart as their own themes.
416: /// `Auto` borrows the dark or light pool depending on the appearance
417: /// [`auto_dark`] resolves — the OS's while it self-switches, the local clock's
418: /// once it is pinned; [`THEME_MODES`] is the list the picker advertises.
419: #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
420: pub enum RandomMode {
421:     Dark,
422:     Light,
423:     Crt,
424:     Auto,
425: }
426: 
427: /// The themes crew offers: three pools plus `auto`, which serves one of them
428: /// per OS appearance. This is the whole user-facing theme list (`/theme`, the
429: /// settings picker, the `Ctrl+Shift+L` cycle); everything else (legacy
430: /// `random-*` / `modern*` names, individual palettes) parses for back-compat
431: /// but isn't advertised.
432: pub const THEME_MODES: [RandomMode; 4] = [
433:     RandomMode::Dark,
434:     RandomMode::Light,
435:     RandomMode::Crt,
436:     RandomMode::Auto,
437: ];

480:     /// Whether `id` belongs to this mode's rotation pool. Every palette lands
481:     /// in exactly ONE of Dark/Light/Crt, decided by two questions in order:
482:     /// is it a phosphor tube ([`ThemeId::is_crt`] — which the modern family's
483:     /// bloom-only `CrtStyle` deliberately does not make it), and if not, is
484:     /// its page dark or light. So each pool is "every palette that looks like
485:     /// this", modern glow and plain paper alike, and a rotation can never flip
486:     /// the page from near-black to near-white. `Auto` serves its
487:     /// per-appearance pairing ([`auto_side`]) — by default the dark or light
488:     /// pool depending on [`auto_dark`], a pinned side being a one-palette
489:     /// pool.
490:     pub fn in_pool(self, id: ThemeId) -> bool {
491:         match self {
492:             RandomMode::Dark => id.is_dark() && !id.is_crt(),
493:             RandomMode::Light => !id.is_dark() && !id.is_crt(),
494:             RandomMode::Crt => id.is_crt(),
495:             RandomMode::Auto => match auto_side() {
496:                 Selection::Mode(m) => m.in_pool(id),
497:                 Selection::Fixed(f) => id == f,
498:             },
499:         }
500:     }
501: }

521: /// Parse a `/theme` argument / config value. The four canonical names are
522: /// `dark`, `light`, `crt`, `auto`; the pre-consolidation names (`random`,
523: /// `random-dark`, `random-light`, and the `modern` / `modern-light` modes
524: /// that are now simply part of `dark` / `light`) and every individual palette
525: /// name still parse so old configs keep loading — a name that stops parsing is
526: /// a config line that silently does nothing, which is exactly the failure this
527: /// list exists to prevent.
528: pub fn parse_selection(s: &str) -> Option<Selection> {
529:     let s = s.trim();
530:     // `modern` was a dark-page rotation and `modern-light` a light-page one;
531:     // both pools were folded into `dark` / `light`, so the old names resolve
532:     // to the pool that swallowed them (a superset — the same palettes still
533:     // come up, alongside the paper ones).
534:     if s.eq_ignore_ascii_case("dark")
535:         || s.eq_ignore_ascii_case("random")
536:         || s.eq_ignore_ascii_case("random-dark")
537:         || s.eq_ignore_ascii_case("modern")
538:         || s.eq_ignore_ascii_case("random-modern")
539:     {
540:         return Some(Selection::Mode(RandomMode::Dark));
541:     }
542:     if s.eq_ignore_ascii_case("light")
543:         || s.eq_ignore_ascii_case("random-light")
544:         || s.eq_ignore_ascii_case("modern-light")
545:         || s.eq_ignore_ascii_case("modern light")
546:         || s.eq_ignore_ascii_case("modernlight")
547:         || s.eq_ignore_ascii_case("random-modern-light")
548:     {
549:         return Some(Selection::Mode(RandomMode::Light));
550:     }
551:     if s.eq_ignore_ascii_case("crt") || s.eq_ignore_ascii_case("random-crt") {
552:         return Some(Selection::Mode(RandomMode::Crt));
553:     }
554:     if s.eq_ignore_ascii_case("auto") {
555:         return Some(Selection::Mode(RandomMode::Auto));
556:     }
557:     ThemeId::from_name(s).map(Selection::Fixed)
558: }
559: 
560: /// The active rotation mode, if any.
561: pub fn mode() -> Option<RandomMode> {
562:     RandomMode::from_u8(MODE.load(Ordering::Relaxed))
563: }
564: 
565: /// Whether any rotation mode is active.
566: pub fn is_random() -> bool {
567:     mode().is_some()
568: }
569: 
570: /// Report the OS appearance (winit ThemeChanged / startup Window::theme).
571: /// While `auto` is active the change takes effect on the next rotation tick;
572: /// callers that want an immediate flip re-apply the selection (the app does).
573: pub fn set_os_dark(dark: bool) {
574:     OS_DARK.store(dark, Ordering::Relaxed);
575: }
576: 
577: /// The last reported OS appearance (defaults to dark).
578: pub fn os_dark() -> bool {
579:     OS_DARK.load(Ordering::Relaxed)
580: }
581: 
582: /// Report whether the OS switches its OWN appearance on a schedule (macOS
583: /// Appearance: Auto). Fed at startup and on every ThemeChanged.
584: pub fn set_os_auto(auto: bool) {
585:     OS_AUTO.store(auto, Ordering::Relaxed);
586: }
587: 
588: /// Whether the OS appearance is self-switching (defaults to `true`: assume
589: /// the OS is authoritative unless crew has been told otherwise).
590: pub fn os_auto() -> bool {
591:     OS_AUTO.load(Ordering::Relaxed)
592: }
593: 
594: /// Report whether the local clock currently reads as daytime.
595: pub fn set_daylight(day: bool) {
596:     DAYLIGHT.store(day, Ordering::Relaxed);
597: }
598: 
599: /// The last reported daylight state (defaults to false = night).
600: pub fn daylight() -> bool {
601:     DAYLIGHT.load(Ordering::Relaxed)
602: }
603: 
604: /// Which half `auto` should serve, as a single yes/no — the ONE place the
605: /// two clocks are weighed against each other, so every caller (pool
606: /// membership, the `/theme` report, the settings blurb) agrees.
607: ///
608: /// While the OS switches itself, the OS wins: it already encodes the user's
609: /// day/night preference, schedule and all. Once the appearance is PINNED,
610: /// following it makes `auto` indistinguishable from `dark` (or `light`)
611: /// forever, so crew falls back to its own light-hours window — which is what
612: /// "light by day, dark by night" says on the tin.
613: pub fn auto_dark() -> bool {
614:     if os_auto() {
615:         os_dark()
616:     } else {
617:         !daylight()
618:     }
619: }
620: 
621: /// What `auto` serves per OS appearance: `.0` while dark, `.1` while light.
622: /// `None` = the built-in pairing (the dark/light paper pool). Read on theme
623: /// application and rotation ticks, not per frame, so a mutex is fine.
624: static AUTO_POOLS: Mutex<(Option<Selection>, Option<Selection>)> = Mutex::new((None, None));
625: 
626: /// Configure `auto`'s per-appearance pairing (config `theme_dark` /
627: /// `theme_light`): each side is a rotation pool (`dark`|`light`|`crt`) or a
628: /// pinned palette — e.g. phosphor tubes at night, light paper by day. A side
629: /// of `auto` itself would recurse and is dropped to the default; `None`
630: /// keeps the built-in paper pool for that appearance.
631: pub fn set_auto_pools(dark: Option<Selection>, light: Option<Selection>) {
632:     let clean = |s: Option<Selection>| s.filter(|s| *s != Selection::Mode(RandomMode::Auto));
633:     *AUTO_POOLS.lock().unwrap() = (clean(dark), clean(light));
634: }
635: 
636: /// The configured pairing itself: `.0` for the dark appearance, `.1` for the
637: /// light one, `None` on a side meaning "the built-in paper pool". Read it to
638: /// TELL the user what `auto` is holding — a side paired for the appearance
639: /// they are not currently in has no other symptom (`theme_light =
640: /// "modern-light"` under a dark OS looks exactly like a setting that does
641: /// nothing at all).
642: pub fn auto_pools() -> (Option<Selection>, Option<Selection>) {
643:     *AUTO_POOLS.lock().unwrap()
644: }
645: 
646: /// `auto`'s light-hours window as minutes past midnight (`.0` start, `.1`
647: /// end), for REPORTING only — the app owns the window, parses it from config
648: /// and decides [`set_daylight`] from it. It lives here beside [`AUTO_POOLS`]
649: /// for the same reason that does: `/theme` has to be able to read back every
650: /// part of what `auto` is holding, and a window it cannot name is a setting
651: /// with no visible effect.
652: static LIGHT_HOURS: Mutex<(u16, u16)> = Mutex::new((7 * 60, 19 * 60));
653: 
654: /// Publish `auto`'s configured light-hours window.
655: pub fn set_light_hours(from: u16, to: u16) {
656:     *LIGHT_HOURS.lock().unwrap() = (from, to);
657: }
658: 
659: /// The configured light-hours window (minutes past midnight).
660: pub fn light_hours() -> (u16, u16) {
661:     *LIGHT_HOURS.lock().unwrap()
662: }
663: 
664: /// The selection `auto` resolves to under the current appearance. Never
665: /// `Mode(Auto)` (see [`set_auto_pools`]), so pool membership can't recurse.
666: pub fn auto_side() -> Selection {
667:     let (dark, light) = *AUTO_POOLS.lock().unwrap();
668:     if auto_dark() {
669:         dark.unwrap_or(Selection::Mode(RandomMode::Dark))
670:     } else {
671:         light.unwrap_or(Selection::Mode(RandomMode::Light))
672:     }
673: }
674: 
675: /// Pick a theme from `mode`'s pool that is NOT `current`, deterministically
676: /// from `seed`. Every pool has exactly 3 entries since the nine-theme cut
677: /// (`every_pool_survives_the_cut` is where that is pinned), so minus `current`
678: /// it is never empty; the `current` filter is skipped only if a future cut
679: /// WOULD empty the pool, which keeps the modulo safe rather than relying on a
680: /// roster size to stay where it is.
681: pub fn random_pick(current: ThemeId, seed: u64, mode: RandomMode) -> ThemeId {
682:     let mut others: Vec<ThemeId> = ALL_THEMES
683:         .iter()
684:         .copied()
685:         .filter(|&t| mode.in_pool(t) && t != current)
686:         .collect();
687:     if others.is_empty() {
688:         others = ALL_THEMES
689:             .iter()
690:             .copied()
691:             .filter(|&t| mode.in_pool(t))
692:             .collect();
693:     }
694:     let idx = (seed.wrapping_mul(6364136223846793005).rotate_right(29) as usize) % others.len();
695:     others[idx]
696: }
697: 
698: /// Apply a parsed selection: a fixed theme pins it (mode off); a mode
699: /// switches immediately to a pick from its pool (so the effect is visible)
700: /// and starts the 10-minute clock.
701: pub fn apply_selection(sel: Selection, now_ms: u64) {
702:     match sel {
703:         Selection::Fixed(id) => {
704:             MODE.store(0, Ordering::Relaxed);
705:             set_theme(id);
706:         }
707:         Selection::Mode(m) => {
708:             MODE.store(m.as_u8(), Ordering::Relaxed);
709:             set_theme(random_pick(current_id(), now_ms, m));
710:             ROTATED_MS.store(now_ms, Ordering::Relaxed);
711:         }
712:     }
713: }
714: 
715: /// The status-line label for the active selection: the mode's name while
716: /// rotating, else the pinned theme's name.
717: pub fn selection_label() -> &'static str {
718:     match mode() {
719:         Some(m) => m.as_str(),
720:         None => current_id().as_str(),
721:     }
722: }
723: 
724: /// Called each poll tick with the current wall-clock ms. When a mode is on
725: /// and `ROTATE_MS` has elapsed, switch to a new pick from the mode's pool
726: /// (auto re-reads the OS appearance every tick) and return `true` so the
727: /// caller repaints. Cheap and lock-free — safe at ~62 Hz on the winit thread.
728: pub fn tick_random(now_ms: u64) -> bool {
729:     let Some(m) = mode() else {
730:         return false;
731:     };
732:     let last = ROTATED_MS.load(Ordering::Relaxed);
733:     if now_ms.saturating_sub(last) < ROTATE_MS {
734:         return false;
735:     }
736:     set_theme(random_pick(current_id(), now_ms, m));
737:     ROTATED_MS.store(now_ms, Ordering::Relaxed);
738:     true
739: }
740: 
741: /// Advance the `Ctrl+Shift+L` cycle one step through [`THEME_MODES`]:
742: /// dark → light → crt → auto → dark, wrapping. Any other state (a pinned
743: /// palette) enters at `dark`. The order IS `THEME_MODES` — walking the list
744: /// rather than hand-writing the successors is what keeps a newly added mode
745: /// from being silently unreachable by the hotkey (which is exactly what
746: /// happened when a fourth pool was added). Returns the status-line label.
747: pub fn cycle_next(now_ms: u64) -> &'static str {
748:     let next = match mode() {
749:         Some(m) => {
750:             let i = THEME_MODES.iter().position(|&x| x == m).unwrap_or(0);
751:             THEME_MODES[(i + 1) % THEME_MODES.len()]
752:         }
753:         None => RandomMode::Dark,
754:     };
755:     apply_selection(Selection::Mode(next), now_ms);
756:     next.as_str()
757: }
758: 
759: /// The lock every test that writes a process-wide theme global takes —
760: /// the selection, the OS appearance, the pole shift. One lock for the whole
761: /// crate rather than one per test file, because the globals are shared: two
762: /// files with two locks would serialise against themselves and race each
763: /// other, which is worse than no lock at all for being harder to see.
764: #[cfg(test)]
765: pub(crate) fn test_guard() -> std::sync::MutexGuard<'static, ()> {
766:     static LOCK: std::sync::Mutex<()> = std::sync::Mutex::new(());
767:     LOCK.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner())
768: }
769: 
770: #[cfg(test)]
771: #[path = "lib_tests.rs"]
772: mod tests;
